item.title: Paper: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
item.description: The authors introduce a framework that moves beyond simple document retrieval by enabling models to compute and synthesize evidence across multiple sources, improving performance on complex reasoning tasks.

item.title: Paper: EngramEdit: Decoupled Knowledge Updates in LLMs through Conditional Memory
item.description: This research explores updating factual knowledge in LLMs by isolating it into a separate memory layer, allowing for targeted updates without needing to retrain the entire model.

item.title: Paper: Document-Level Text Simplification in Estonian Using Large Language Models
item.description: This study evaluates how well current LLMs handle document-level text simplification in Estonian, providing insights for applying language models to low-resource, morphologically complex languages.

item.title: Paper: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
item.description: The researchers demonstrate that robotic world models follow predictable scaling laws, allowing practitioners to better estimate the compute and data needed to improve robot planning capabilities.

item.title: Paper: Towards In-Parameter Memory Augmentation for Large Language Models
item.description: This paper proposes updating model parameters to store external knowledge, providing a more efficient alternative to long-context prompting for LLMs that need to retain domain-specific information.

item.title: Paper: MINDSET: Energy-based Schema Evolution for Long Conversational Agent Memory
item.description: The authors introduce a memory management system for conversational agents that dynamically updates stored information to ensure context remains relevant as user needs evolve over time.

item.title: Paper: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively
item.description: Sherpa is a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes LLM teaching strategies based on real-time student performance, moving beyond static pedagogical rules for personalized education.

item.title: Paper: Agent in a Bottle: Can LLM Agents Turn Their Capabilities Into Cheap, Scalable Artifacts?
item.description: This research explores how LLM agents can autonomously distill their problem-solving skills into smaller, cheaper models to handle high-volume tasks without incurring high API costs.

item.title: Paper: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
item.description: This paper introduces a meta-reasoning framework that helps AI agents manage complex workflows by explicitly deciding when to continue, restart, or pivot during task execution.

item.title: Paper: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
item.description: The researchers developed a method for AI models to automatically build better execution environments for other models, improving performance without needing to retrain the underlying weights.

item.title: Paper: Breaking the Uniformity Trap: Scaling Video Diffusion Model via SplitMoE
item.description: The authors propose a specialized Mixture-of-Experts architecture for video models that avoids inefficient token routing, leading to better handling of complex, redundant visual data.

item.title: Paper: Do LLM Agents Execute the Plans They Declare? From Planning-Mode Declaration to Pattern-Specific Execution
item.description: This study investigates why LLM agents often fail to follow their own plans, proposing a routing system that forces agents to explicitly declare and stick to specific planning strategies.

item.title: Paper: Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL

item.title: Paper: A Unified Uncertainty Representation for Graph Neural Networks via Doubly-Spectral Stochastic Expansion
